text: **KnowLP-RAG**（DSH 的 MCP 与原生 Cordis 插件）：把 Markdown 笔记建立为可检索的知识图谱，并将检索结果提供给 DSH agent。MCP 入口注册搜索、笔记读取、反馈和状态等工具；原生插件还能在每轮提示时自动检索并注入相关笔记。主要功能包括多引擎知识检索、按文本/PDF/图像/Office/代码类型检索、读取笔记和记录检索反馈，适合希望让 agent 查找个人 Markdown 知识库的用户。需要配置笔记目录 KNOWLP_VAULT 和索引目录 KNOWLP_GRAPH_DIR；MCP 启动需要 Node 与 Python 环境。

KnowLP-RAG connects a Markdown knowledge graph to DSH through MCP and a native Cordis plugin. Agents can search notes, read results, and record feedback; the native plugin can also inject relevant notes into each turn. Set KNOWLP_VAULT and KNOWLP_GRAPH_DIR; MCP needs Node and Python.
想让 DSH agent 能搜索我自己的 Markdown 笔记库。
有没有办法把相关笔记自动放进每轮对话的上下文？
我想按 PDF、图片或代码文件类型检索知识库。
DSH 能不能根据搜索结果记录哪些笔记真正有用？
I want my DSH agent to search my Markdown notes and show the most relevant files.
Can search results from my knowledge base be injected into each conversation turn?
Help me retrieve notes by file type, including PDFs and images.
I need a way to mark which retrieved notes were useful.
**KnowLP-RAG** 的功能「知识检索」：通过 knowlp_search 对配置的笔记库执行多引擎检索，合并排序结果并返回命中的笔记。MCP 调用者提交查询和结果数量。
**KnowLP-RAG** 的功能「按资料类型检索」：调用 knowlp_search_pools 并指定 text、pdf、image、office 或 code 类型，返回相应资料池的检索结果及状态。
**KnowLP-RAG** 的功能「对话内自动召回」：原生 Cordis 插件在新一轮用户消息时检索相关笔记，并把结果作为上下文快照注入 agent。

@eqman00003/knowlp-rag README · KnowLP-RAG：**Agent-first knowledge retrieval** — turn your Markdown notes into a self-maintaining knowledge graph that is "use it or lose it". Agents (DSH / Claude Code) install, build the graph, and self-check it; only the vault path must be provided by the human. Retrieval returns reading paths: which notes to read, in what order, and which are similar substitutes.

export KNOWLP_GRAPH_DIR="$HOME/.knowlp-dsh"    # writable index directory

@eqman00003/knowlp-rag README · Seven tools：| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `knowlp_search` | Four-engine fan-out retrieval (dual-graph P/S-Agent + vector + full-text) |
| `knowlp_get_note` | Read note content (read-only, path-traversal safe) |
| `knowlp_stats` | Engine/graph health self-check (first stop for troubleshooting) |
| `knowlp_status` | Index lifecycle status (missing/fresh/stale + reason + exact fix command) |
| `knowlp_record_feedback` | Explicit feedback (the only entry point of the weight loop) |
| `knowlp_record_correction` | Explicit preference pairs (chosen ≻ rejected) — the input to preference learning |
| `skill_search` | Skill index retrieval |

@eqman00003/knowlp-rag README · PixelRAG (optional cross-machine visual retrieval)：PixelRAG is an optional **visual-retrieval** engine — it embeds visual content
for retrieval instead of relying on text tokens alone. It runs on a **separate
GPU machine** on your network: the agent offloads the visual-embedding work to
that box over Tailscale rather than computing it on the laptop. Retrieval falls
back through three tiers:

@eqman00003/knowlp-rag README · PixelRAG (optional cross-machine visual retrieval)：1. **desktop GPU** — the primary dedicated box (an RTX-class machine reachable over Tailscale)
2. **local** — a same-machine fallback
3. **cloud API** — a hosted PixelRAG endpoint

Configure it via `KNOWLP_PIXELRAG_DESKTOP` / `pixelrag_local`. Unconfigured, it stays off — retrieval still works in n-gram / embedding mode.

@eqman00003/knowlp-rag README · PixelRAG (optional cross-machine visual retrieval)：> **Reproducing this**: it is deployment-specific — you need your own GPU machine running a PixelRAG service, a network path to it (e.g. Tailscale), and its endpoint address. No bundled service ships with KnowLP.
@eqman00003/knowlp-rag README · Why KnowLP?：Grep for "RAG architecture" gives you 105 files. KnowLP gives you 3 ranked hits with dependency context.

@eqman00003/knowlp-rag README · Why KnowLP?：| | `grep` | Naive vector store | **KnowLP** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Result ranking | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Dependency chain (P-Agent) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Similar substitutes (S-Agent) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Works without GPU | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ (n-gram mode) |
| Improves with use (feedback) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (weight loop) |
| Paragraph-level matching | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Decay & forgetting (use it or lose it) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (three half-life tiers) |

@eqman00003/knowlp-rag README · Why KnowLP?：**The difference**: vector search finds documents that "contain keywords"; KnowLP finds documents you *should read given your query*, with reading paths. Edge weights between notes evolve with usage — consumed edges strengthen, unused edges decay by half-life (ephemeral 1 day / default 30 days / declarative never).

Works with Chinese note vaults out of the box (Chinese time-anchor queries and Chinese full-text search are supported).

pip install -e ".[mcp,modeling]" pytest pypdf
python -m pytest -q
```

Nothing in the suite needs a GPU, a real Office install, or a private vault, so
**CI runs all of it** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, on every push and PR).

@eqman00003/knowlp-rag README · Tests：| Layer | What it covers | In CI |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_packaging_closure.py` | The two manifests against the real import graph: **every** top-level module is covered, and everything the MCP entry can reach is in npm `files`. A deliberately empty `files` entry turns it red and names the importers. | yes |
| the rest of `tests/` | Retrieval and routing, dual graph, modality pools, the preference loop, evidence/result contracts, and a real MCP stdio integration test. | yes |
| the skips | Four need symlink privileges (developer mode on Windows). The fifth — the real-vault parity case — only runs when `KNOWLP_VAULT` points at a real vault. | — |

@eqman00003/knowlp-rag README · Tests：Against a real vault locally: `303 passed, 4 skipped`. On CI, where the vault is
deliberately unreachable: `302 passed, 5 skipped`. The one test difference is the
real-vault parity case, and it says so in the skip reason.

`test_packaging_closure.py` exists because 3.0.10 shipped without it: the npm
tarball was missing 16 top-level modules, six of them in the MCP entry's import
closure, and `knowlp_search` could not run at all from an npm install.
